questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location, country, courses available

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Some things were well introduced and other things I didn't find out about until halfway through my stay. It would've been great to have a specific contact person at the host university to talk to.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was hard and expensive and we ended in a different area than originally intended (but loved it). Go on furnished finder and create an agent. FT the hosts beforehand.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of activities on campus that are cool, but most people living on campus are 18-20 years old and not an old 18-20.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: On campus options were pretty unattractive to me, due to costs, not having full kitchen or any private space.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to find your "registration window" on your own and during that time log in and find the classes you wanted. For nearly all my classes I found out very late that I should fill out a pre-req because in their system I looked like a freshman. I did, but because I wasn't aware ahead of time I ended up far down on waitlists and this changed what classes I ended up taking.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I emailed several people about my standing, for various reasons. It was never changed, but I ended up being able to enroll in some relevant courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly so. There was one course I was really sad to miss out on, but otherwise I ended up being happy with my courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find your registration window early, fill out and send pre-reqs as soon as you can.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took some lower and some upperdivision courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mostly the teaching was not mixed styles. At KU the same course will have both lectures and seminars. At UCSD it was either or, which I didn't prefer. There was also a less close relationship between teachers and students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on daytrips into nature or smaller cities like Solvang, Joshua Tree, TJ. Find local events and go to every farmers market in existence.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: give them compliments or wear things worthy of compliments. Take initiative.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Customs at restaurants and stores (greetings, paying etc). 
Personal space.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Appreciating nature, social cultural awareness of issues like colonialism, racism and the existence of trans people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Live by the beach, get a car, enjoy the nature.
